options.label: A
options.truth: False for the short parenthesized, position-based form described here: values normally come from component1(), component2() in order; the current official page also documents experimental name-based forms, so the option's categorical wording ignores that mode.
options.refutation: In position-based destructuring variable names do not select components; name-based destructuring is a separately enabled experimental feature.
options.ansc: PASS: makes a direct claim about how component selection works and fully addresses the question, despite being wrong for the ordinary form.
options.sfpl: FAIL: ‘а вовсе не’ adds emphatic contrast; broadly similar declarative shape to B/C.

options.label: B
options.truth: False: any right-hand value with the required callable component functions can be destructured; data classes are only one convenient source of generated componentN functions.
options.refutation: Kotlin documentation says any value with the required component functions qualifies, and illustrates Pair, map entries, and custom types.
options.ansc: PASS: states an eligibility rule that answers the operation's applicability; no broader catalog is required by the question.
options.sfpl: FAIL: uses categorical exclusivity and emphatic ‘решительно’, a conspicuous tone signal.
options.ru: PASS: understandable; ‘решительно ни с каким другим типом’ is rhetorically heavy but clear.

options.label: C
options.truth: False as a universal claim: reordering same-typed components can compile and silently change meanings, while incompatible explicit or downstream types can cause compilation errors.
options.refutation: Data-class componentN order follows primary-constructor property order; consequences depend on component and use-site types, so neither guaranteed error nor guaranteed silent success holds.
options.ansc: PASS: directly answers a consequence of how destructuring works; this is a complete response to the visible question's broad ‘how’ wording.
options.sfpl: FAIL: uniquely predicts a downstream consequence and is longer/more specific than A/B; its categorical future-error phrasing stands out.

options.label: D
options.truth: True: a declaration such as val (a,b)=value is compiled to calls to component1() and component2(), which must be operator functions.
options.refutation: The official language page gives this desugaring and says any value works if the required component functions can be called.
options.ansc: PASS: direct and complete core mechanism answer.
options.sfpl: FAIL: uniquely provides the compiler transformation and API names, making it more explanatory and technically specific than the distractors.

sections.assessment: Correctly states positional correspondence for the ordinary form, but does not mention the official page's experimental name-based alternative.
Names the suspected property-name model but does not explain why a reader might infer it.
A direct consequence follows: reordering would preserve named matches, making the positional-order risk disappear.
Accurately names component1/component2 order for positional destructuring, while leaving the experimental named mode unstated.
Correctly says destructuring can use any type providing the necessary componentN functions.
Restates the misconception without giving its likely source, such as data classes generating componentN automatically.
The proposed consequence is coherent: if only data classes worked, users would not need to define componentN for other types.
operator componentN functions suffice for the needed components, though the number required depends on destructured arity.
‘Молча читает не те значения’ is not universal: identical component types can silently swap meanings, but incompatible explicit types or use can yield compile errors.
Identifies the mistaken expectation that the compiler catches reordering but does not explain why that expectation arises.
Suggests a benefit of compiler detection but does not specify which class of bugs would be prevented.
Calling positional reordering a ‘тихий баг’ overgeneralizes; only compatible types and uses can let a semantic swap pass silently.
Accurately describes the component1/component2 expansion and eligibility by componentN availability.
Shows declaration and loop syntax, but uses ellipses and omits actual User/map definitions or the resulting values.
Clearly describes the common use of unpacking one value into variables.
Correctly states position-based mapping, though the official reference now also has an experimental name-based mode.
Correctly notes data classes generate componentN functions automatically from primary-constructor properties in declaration order.

axes.SEMANTICS: PASS_WITH_QUALIFICATION — D is correct for the described syntax; A and D must be scoped against newly documented experimental name-based destructuring.
axes.ANSC: PASS — each option gives a full claim responsive to ‘how’; A/B concern selection/eligibility, C consequence, D mechanism. B is broad but answers applicability; no unspecified catalog is needed.
axes.SFPL: FAIL — D alone presents the direct desugaring and API names; C alone predicts a specific consequence; B/C use emphatic/categorical forms, while A/C/D are fluent declaratives.
axes.RU: PASS — all four options are understandable Russian; B is emphatic and C's absolute claim is a factual scope problem rather than a language defect.
axes.FACTS: FAIL — C's section explanation states an absolute silent outcome that ignores incompatible types; A and D omit the newly documented experimental name-based feature when phrased categorically.
axes.SECTIONS: FAIL — A/B/C wrong explanations vary in specificity; C.what_actually and C.how_it_should_be overgeneralize; D has fuller explanatory treatment.
axes.LINKAGE: PASS — all options concern mechanics, eligibility, or consequences of destructuring under the visible question.

theory_review: Current theory accurately covers position-based destructuring, componentN calls, member/extension functions, data-class generation, skipped components, and conditional reorder outcomes. The opened official destructuring page now also documents experimental name-based destructuring, so theory's categorical statement that variable names never affect selection requires a version/feature qualification.
limits: Current official documentation labels name-based destructuring experimental and describes compiler-option modes; this review does not verify compiler-version availability or project configuration beyond that page.
Reordering outcomes depend on static component types, explicit variable types, and later use; no single outcome applies to every code change.
This review covers Q31 and its 17 supplied sections only.
